reason: The text explicitly demonstrates that helping the Hebrew people is central to Yahweh's stated goals. When the Hebrews cry out in bondage, 'God heard their cry' (וַיִּשְׁמַע אֱלֹהִים אֶת־נַאֲקָתָם) and 'remembered His covenant' (וַיִּזְכֹּר אֱלֹהִים אֶת־בְּרִיתוֹ). God then explicitly tells Moses: 'I will bring you out from under the burdens of Egypt, and I will rescue you from their bondage, and I will redeem you with an outstretched arm' (וְהוֹצֵאתִי אֶתְכֶם...וְהִצַּלְתִּי אֶתְכֶם...וְגָאַלְתִּי אֶתְכֶם). Furthermore, God promises to take them as His people (וְלָקַחְתִּי אֶתְכֶם לִי לְעָם) and to bring them into the Promised Land (וְהֵבֵאתִי אֶתְכֶם אֶל־הָאָרֶץ). These statements constitute explicit divine goals regarding the welfare and liberation of the Hebrew people.
